submission.natural_language_explanation: Fires on the word itself (strongest as an attributive modifier) when it names a sectarian, ethnic-insurgent or non-state armed-faction identity: Shiite, Sunni, Kurdish, Houthi, Salafi, separatist, insurgent, guerrilla, rebel (even non-political 'teenage rebel'), militant, militia, paramilitary, Islamist, jihadist, Maoist (roughly 0.5-1.2 x max), with weaker firing on extremist and on the following head noun (cleric, fighters, militia, group ~0.05-0.4). It stays at zero on mainstream religious or national identities (Muslim, Christian, Catholic, Jewish, Palestinian, Canadian), on neutral group words (opposition, student, government, advocacy), on 'Islamic State', and mostly on 'terrorist'/'armed'/'radical' (below 0.2); ordinary text has no floor (zero everywhere), and the effect is lexical, not dependent on Middle-East news context.
